    * Keyword anchors blockquote: greatest least NULL Trino, greatest returns NULL, least NULL argument, greatest vs Postgres, do all engines greatest least behave the same, ignore NULL greatest, COALESCE greatest, porting Postgres greatest to Trino, greatest cross-engine, least cross-engine. Verified date 2026-06-07.
    * One-fact summary: Trino + Oracle + MySQL + BigQuery — NULL if ANY arg NULL. Postgres — IGNORES NULLs, returns NULL only if ALL args NULL. `GREATEST(1, NULL, 5)` = 5 in Postgres but NULL in Trino. So 'all engines behave the same' is FALSE — Postgres is the outlier.
    * VERBATIM Trino docs quote: 'Like most other functions in Trino, they return null if any argument is null. Note that in some other databases, such as PostgreSQL, they only return null if all arguments are null.' (trino.io/docs/467/functions/comparison.html, fetched 2026-06-07.)
    * VERBATIM Postgres docs quote: 'NULL values in the argument list are ignored. The result will be NULL only if all the expressions evaluate to NULL.' (postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-conditional.html, fetched 2026-06-07.)
    * COALESCE-each-arg workaround for Postgres-like behavior in Trino: greatest(coalesce(a, 0), coalesce(b, 0), coalesce(c, 0)) with floor=0 for greatest; least with ceiling sentinel. Two-arg null-passthrough CASE variant.
    * 4-row DO-NOT-WRITE: (1) 'greatest/least ignore NULLs in Trino' FALSE; (2) 'Postgres and Trino greatest/least behave identically on NULL' FALSE; (3) 'all SQL engines treat greatest/least NULLs the same' FALSE (engine-specific; Postgres is outlier); (4) NEW load-bearing — 'COALESCE(greatest(a, b, c), 0) reproduces Postgres semantics' FALSE (outer COALESCE only fires when WHOLE expression is NULL, not when SOME args are NULL; you must wrap EACH arg).
    * Cross-ref to r27 §4.4D (the deep Oracle-migration canonical with worked migration examples).
